   • r23:884 keyword anchors block: `drop exact duplicate rows, remove duplicate rows where every column is identical, whole-row dedup, dedup entire row, delete fully duplicated rows, rows that are byte-identical, SELECT DISTINCT *, DISTINCT star, dedup all columns, remove exact duplicates, de-duplicate identical rows, PARTITION BY *, ROW_NUMBER over all columns, dedup without a key.` Comprehensive anchor coverage for the search keywords.
   • r23:886 THE ONE-FACT SUMMARY: `To drop EXACT duplicate rows — rows where every column is identical — the simplest and correct Trino tool is SELECT DISTINCT *. The Trino SELECT docs say verbatim: "If the argument DISTINCT is specified, only unique rows are included in the result set." DISTINCT * applies that uniqueness across all columns of the row, so byte-identical rows collapse to one. This is a different problem from "one row per KEY" (the ROW_NUMBER() canonical above) — for exact whole-row dedup you do not need a window function at all.`

Worked example r07:1392-1396: `SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') AS local_day_et, COUNT(*) AS signups FROM signups WHERE created_at >= date_trunc('day', current_timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') - INTERVAL '30' DAY GROUP BY date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')`.
   • r07:1402 BARE-TIMESTAMP GOTCHA — for a column typed `TIMESTAMP` (no time zone) carrying UTC-intent, AT TIME ZONE ATTACHES the zone label without converting; chain `AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'` (first attach UTC, then convert). On a true `timestamp with time zone` value, AT TIME ZONE CONVERTS the same instant to the target wall-clock.
   • r27:837 ROUTING: `Core semantic to memorize. expr AT TIME ZONE 'zone' does NOT change the underlying instant — it re-renders the same UTC moment with a different zone label attached. The Trino docs example: timestamp '2012-10-31 01:00 UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles' → 2012-10-30 18:00:00.000 America/Los_Angeles.`
   • r27:781-794 ALTERNATIVES catalog: (1) `SET TIME ZONE 'zone'` dedicated command (session); (2) `sql.forced-session-time-zone` server config (cluster-level); (3) `expr AT TIME ZONE 'zone'` per-expression (recommended for dbt — explicit at call site). Three forms findable.
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch at trino.io/docs/current/functions/datetime.html): 
     – `AT TIME ZONE` operator: "The AT TIME ZONE operator sets the time zone of a timestamp" — example: `SELECT timestamp '2012-10-31 01:00 UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'; -- 2012-10-30 18:00:00.000 America/Los_Angeles`. 
     – `with_timezone(timestamp(p), zone) → timestamp(p) with time zone`: "Returns the timestamp specified in timestamp with the time zone specified in zone with precision p." Useful for ATTACHING a zone to a bare timestamp (equivalent to AT TIME ZONE on a bare timestamp). 
     – `from_unixtime(unixtime, zone) → timestamp(3) with time zone`: takes epoch-seconds + zone, returns timestamp with that zone attached. Useful when source is epoch-seconds AND you want a specific zone in one step. 
     – `from_unixtime(unixtime, hours, minutes) → timestamp(3) with time zone`: takes epoch + zone offset (hours, minutes), returns timestamptz at that fixed offset (no DST awareness — prefer the IANA zone form). 
     All matches existing r07:1377+ / r27:765+ resource content verbatim. No edits needed.

=== DOCS-TRUTH SUMMARY (verified 2026-06-08 via trino.io/docs/current via WebFetch) ===
• AT TIME ZONE — `The AT TIME ZONE operator sets the time zone of a timestamp` — example `timestamp '2012-10-31 01:00 UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles' → 2012-10-30 18:00:00.000 America/Los_Angeles`. On timestamptz: CONVERTS. On bare timestamp: ATTACHES the zone without converting. ✓ (matches r07:1402 + r27:837 verbatim)
• with_timezone(ts(p), zone) → timestamp(p) with time zone — returns ts with the zone attached. ATTACH semantics, equivalent to AT TIME ZONE on a bare timestamp. ✓ (consistent with r27 ATTACH-vs-CONVERT semantics)
• from_unixtime(unixtime, zone) → timestamp(3) with time zone — epoch-seconds to ts-with-zone in one step. ✓
• from_unixtime(unixtime, hours, minutes) → timestamp(3) with time zone — fixed-offset variant (no DST). ✓
• approx_most_frequent(buckets, value, capacity) → map<[same as value], bigint> — three args (BIGINT buckets, value, BIGINT capacity); returns MAP from value to estimated frequency. To extract a single mode: MAP_KEYS(approx_most_frequent(1, col, 100))[1]. ✓ (matches r23:661 verbatim signature)
• SELECT DISTINCT: `If the argument DISTINCT is specified, only unique rows are included in the result set.` SELECT DISTINCT * applies uniqueness across the entire row — the canonical exact-whole-row-dedup form. ✓ (matches r23:886 verbatim)
• All Aggregate functions can be used as window functions by adding the OVER clause — SUM(x) OVER, AVG(x) OVER, COUNT(x) OVER all valid. ✓ (matches r07:1626 verbatim)
